source.title: Bayesian WeakS-to-Strong from Text Classification to Generation
source.authors: Zi-Yun Cui; Zi-Yang Zhang; Wen Wu; Guang-Zhi Sun; Chao Zhang

record.file_problem: none; the full paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: Runs weak-to-strong fine-tuning and reports PGR, including single weak supervisors and strong students, on new tasks and model settings. It also tests changes to the training and supervision methods.
record.gate_note: Rows record reported PGR results. The paper also reports weak-model agreement in Figure 3, but this is agreement among weak models, not error similarity between weak supervisors and strong students. Table 1 and Table 3 provide the true-label ceilings and weak-model reference scores used for PGR; they are not separate weak-to-strong intervention results.
record.test_reason: On SciQ binary classification the study repeats the Burns et al. recipe: weak supervisors fine-tuned on ground truth, a Qwen-7B student trained on weak labels, and PGR reported with and without the auxiliary confidence loss. It extends this to CosmosQA (T3), to SLURP slot-filling generation with Llama-2-7B (T2/T3), and to multi-weak ensembling and cDPO, all changes to training (V2). Its results bear directly on V1, V2 and V3.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, with two corrections. First, the Bayesian method recovers only part of the gap, not 'strong-model performance': best PGR is 0.828 on SciQ and 0.668 on SLURP. Second, the authors do not claim Bayesian aggregation alone is more robust. They argue that Naive and Bayesian Multi-Weak are both more robust than Joint Decoding to one poor weak model, and that aux loss helps Bayesian but not naive approaches on generation. cDPO gives a small further gain (0.705).
record.recipe_differences: Uses weak-model labels to fine-tune stronger pretrained students and reports PGR, but extends the setup with multiple weak supervisors, evidential Bayesian estimation, sequence-generation supervision, and cDPO; the evaluated tasks and models differ from Burns et al.
record.method_sensitivity: Results depend on task, weak supervisor or ensemble size, auxiliary-loss use, and weak-label aggregation method. In the SLURP Joint Decoding appendix, the authors also report sensitivity to weak-model quality and beam size, but detailed appendix rows were not extracted.

fits_no_version.finding: Agreement among weak models is about 0.74–0.78 on classification and at most 0.56 on generation (Figure 3). The authors offer this as the reason ensembling helps.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Diversity or low agreement among multiple weak supervisors enables ensemble gains in weak-to-strong PGR.

record.problems: Only three and five weak supervisors were tested; the authors cite computational-resource limits. SLURP single-supervisor estimates show substantial variability, including large standard deviations. Experiments cover two task types and do not test distribution shift or error similarity between weak and strong models.
record.rows_left_out: Within the 60-row limit, omitted the two CosmosQA single-supervisor results for GPT2-Large without auxiliary loss and OPT-1.3B without auxiliary loss (Table 7). Also omitted the separate weak-model weighting comparisons (Table 9), Joint Decoding weak-model-combination and beam-size sweeps (Tables 10-11), and weak-model agreement matrices (Figure 3). Figure 3 agreement is among weak models, not the strong-versus-weak error similarity named in V4.

untested.parts: No student- or supervisor-size sweep (all weak models are 0.8–1.4B, students about 7B). No chess or reward modelling. No representation analysis or predictor of PGR.
Entire version. No test of exploiting unverifiable errors or of distribution shift. Figure 3 measures weak–weak agreement, not weak–strong error similarity.
No sweep of the auxiliary-loss weight γ_max. No loss variants beyond those listed.

record.verdict_notes: Not an original source. For multi-weak runs, PGR is the average of per-weak-model PGRs, which is not directly comparable to single-supervisor PGR. SLURP SDs are very large (up to ±0.715), so many SLURP comparisons are inconclusive. Weak accuracy does not predict PGR on SLURP: TinyLlama has the second-highest weak F1 (0.676) but PGR 0. Rows left out (Tables 9–11, two CosmosQA rows) are declared. Among them, Joint Decoding with M=10 and 5 weak models gives PGR -0.224 ± 0.050, a further V1 failure in generation.

versions.untested_parts: No results on other tasks or model families beyond those reported.
Tests auxiliary loss, multi-weak methods, token probability estimation, and cDPO. Does not test every possible loss variant.

Tests classification and slot filling, several weak model identities, and three versus five weak supervisors. No systematic student- or supervisor-size sweep, chess or reward modelling, or representation analysis.
Does not test strong students exploiting what supervisors cannot check, distribution shift, or whether error similarity between weak and strong models reduces gains.
No theoretical conditions for students to beat supervisors.
No vision experiments; vision work is cited only.

source_check.notes: Reported PGRs are reproduced faithfully, but some paper cells are internally inconsistent: Table 4 TinyLlama accuracy and its weak baseline do not yield the printed zero PGR; Tables 6–7 also disagree for CosmosQA GPT2-Large. Uncertainties are SDs across three seeds; overlapping SDs alone do not establish statistical significance or its absence.

statements.correction: SciQ Table 2: PGR 0.421–0.828. CosmosQA Table 7: full range 0.073–0.571; 0.162–0.571 excludes GPT2-Large. SLURP Table 4: multi-weak range 0.037–0.668; selected successful conditions start at 0.318. Table 5: cDPO raises 0.668 to 0.705. Classification student Qwen-7B; generation student Llama-2-7B; generation uses token-level soft-label estimation.
statements.problem: The ranges summarize selected successful conditions, while the conditions describe naive hard-label fine-tuning. They include auxiliary loss, Bayesian aggregation, soft sequence labels and a post-SFT cDPO result.

statements.correction: C1: Qwen-7B, CosmosQA, GPT2-Large supervision with auxiliary loss; PGR 0.073 ± 0.032; small positive recovery. Remove this study's citation from this statement.
statements.problem: The cited C1 row does not support any of the listed task/model results or an absent/reversed V1 effect.

statements.correction: G20: Joint Decoding-5 with auxiliary loss, PGR 0.091 ± 0.066, limits_scope. G3, G9, G10, G19 and A1 support the absent/reversed condition group. Methods include auxiliary loss, Joint Decoding and a one-hot-label ablation.
statements.problem: The SLURP numbers are correct, but G20 is small positive recovery rather than absent/reversed; the listed methods are not uniformly naive fine-tuning.

statements.correction: S10: Qwen-7B, SciQ, TinyLlama supervision; auxiliary loss raises PGR 0.603 ± 0.024 to 0.643 ± 0.030, a small gain. C1: Qwen-7B, CosmosQA, GPT2-Large supervision; 0.077 ± 0.032 to 0.073 ± 0.032, no auxiliary-loss gain.
statements.problem: This study is cited through S10 and C1 but omitted from the stated evidence and conditions; those rows also warrant different condition-specific readings.

statements.correction: Section 4.1: SLURP supervision uses token-level soft labels estimated across different tokenizers. Qwen-7B is fixed across SciQ and CosmosQA; SLURP uses Llama-2-7B.
statements.problem: The numerical cells and model identities are correct, but the hard-label description does not describe the paper's default sequence-generation supervision.

statements.correction: SciQ tests a fixed Qwen-7B student with supervisors of 0.8B, 1.1B, 1.3B and 1.4B across different families. CosmosQA tests 0.8B, 1.3B and 1.4B supervisors. No within-family supervisor-size sweep isolates size from model identity.
statements.problem: The narrow size range does not establish that fewer than three supervisor sizes were tested; the missing experiment is a controlled size sweep.

statements.correction: CosmosQA: full PGR range 0.073–0.571; 0.162–0.571 excludes GPT2-Large. Appendix E examines soft-label probability estimation; Appendix G links Joint Decoding failure to TinyLlama scoring and beam size. These analyses do not fully explain every single-supervisor failure.
statements.problem: The CosmosQA range excludes GPT2-Large conditions and needs that qualification. The paper investigates generation failures rather than leaving their causes entirely unexplored.
